---
title: "SIS / ISIS screening for high dimensional models"
description: "Fast screening and sparse joint refitting for ultrahigh-dimensional data."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(L0glm)
options(width=90, digits=3)
```

**SIS** stands for **Sure Independence Screening** and **ISIS** for
**Iterative Sure Independence Screening**. These methods rapidly prescreen the
most promising predictors, after which L0glm performs joint sparse selection
and estimation. This combination gives excellent stability in high dimensional
examples and scales well to very large predictor sets. SIS was introduced by
[Fan & Lv (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00674.x), and
[Fan, Samworth & Wu (2009)](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v10/fan09a.html)
developed the general likelihood-based ISIS framework. L0glm uses an offset-based
screen followed by joint sparse refitting; the controls are documented in
[`sis_glm()`](../reference/sis_glm.html).

ISIS is enabled by default for ultrahigh-dimensional models through
`screen="auto"`. Let \(n\) be the number of observations and
\(p_{\mathrm{eligible}}\) the number of eligible predictors. Automatic ISIS
is enabled when

\[
p_{\mathrm{eligible}}>10n.
\]

Screening keeps the full fitting interface while concentrating joint fitting
on a small, informative candidate set. Use `screen="ISIS"` to request it
explicitly at any design size.

## SIS or ISIS in one call

`screen="SIS"` performs one marginal screen. `screen="ISIS"` repeats screening
against the current model, incorporating its predictions as offsets, and keeps
the best joint-fitting round. `screen="auto"` enables ISIS for ultrahigh-dimensional
designs. `screen="none"` fits the supplied design directly.

```{r quick}
set.seed(31)
X <- matrix(rnorm(250*5000), 250, 5000)
beta <- numeric(5000); beta[c(5, 50, 500)] <- c(2, -1.5, 1)
y <- as.numeric(X %*% beta) + rnorm(250)
fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic",
  screen="ISIS", screen.nthreads=2L, relaxed=TRUE)
L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]
```

`nsis` controls a SIS retained set or an ISIS batch. The default ISIS batch is
GIC-based. A small batch lets joint fitting remove false positives as the search
progresses. Screening is implemented in Rcpp with OpenMP and supports ordinary
GLMs, negative binomial, multinomial and Cox models.

`fit$screening` records selected predictors, screening rounds, elapsed time and
thread use. By default screening uses all physical cores, with one thread as
the fallback when detection is unavailable. Explicit `screen.nthreads` values
remain available. Coefficients always have the original dimensions, with zeros for
predictors excluded by screening.

## A million-variable example

This simulation has 500 observations, one million standard-normal predictors
and 60 nonzero effects of either sign. The dense design occupies about 4 GB.

```{r million, eval=FALSE}
n <- 500L
p <- 1000000L
set.seed(123)
X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p)
active <- sample.int(p, 60L)
beta <- numeric(p)
beta[active] <- runif(60L, -.8, .8)
set.seed(1)
y <- as.numeric(X[, active] %*% beta[active]) + rnorm(n)

fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic",
  screen="ISIS", screen.nthreads=8L, nthreads=1L,
  intercept=FALSE, relaxed=TRUE)
L0glm.metrics(fit, beta_true=beta)[c("gic", "TP", "FP", "FN", "TN", "F1_score", "MCC")]
```

The default fit recovers 40 true effects with 3 false positives. Screening uses
all detected physical cores by default (eight on this workstation). Five-fold-CV LASSO took **123.13 s**,
recovering 17 true effects with 50 false positives. The
[benchmark article](performance.html#one-million-predictor-example) reports all methods,
including relaxed LASSO, together with their tuning settings.

## GIC tuning and cross-validation

```{r tuning, eval=FALSE}
gic <- L0glm.tune(X, y, family=gaussian(), screen="ISIS",
  screen.nthreads=8L, tune="gic", nlambda=10, relaxed=TRUE)
cv <- L0glm.tune(X, y, family=gaussian(), screen="ISIS",
  screen.nthreads=8L, tune="cv", nfolds=5, nlambda=10, relaxed=TRUE)
```

Each fold screens its training observations independently. Validation can also
compare a batch grid, for example `nsis=c(2L, 5L, 10L)` with
`validation=list(X=V, y=v)`, while retaining the default GIC batch when `nsis=NULL`.
